attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s ruling on FAC-RESIDUAL-TRUST-UNGATED: if a residual can change whether an argument establishes its conclusion it must be promoted into a typed object and referenced structurally, and a settled argument may not rest on free text as an unstated premise. The rule avoids phrase lists, use-versus-mention and natural-language subsumption entirely. THE CENSUS IS NO LONGER STATED HERE — check-mosaic §13 derives RESIDUAL_ARG_TOTAL, RESIDUAL_SETTLED_WITH_TRUST, RESIDUAL_TYPED and RESIDUAL_UNTYPED from the argument registry and the ledger’s own _settled vocabulary, and the brief substitutes them. INV-R9.3 typed the census three times and got three different pairs, and under that lay a worse fault: `settled` had three definitions in this artifact, so GPT-5.6 hand-counted one number and two local sets here produced two others. ONE typed residual exists as the pattern: ARG-GATE-CLOSURE-COVERAGE carries residual_refs [ASM-STATIC-IMPORT-CLOSURE], the assumption that makes RECEIPT-BINDS-IMPORT-CLOSURE CONDITIONAL.
attrs.gap: MOST ARGUMENTS STILL CARRY UNTYPED RESIDUALS and the field is unenforced, so the pattern is a demonstration and not a rule. Until the gate refuses an untyped residual on a settled argument, FAC-RESIDUAL-TRUST-UNGATED stays open in the form INV-R9.2 stated it. The count is in mosaic/derived/brief-facts.json and deliberately not here.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §10. Assurance 2.0 (arXiv:2405.15800) is the neighbourhood: an undeveloped defeater leaves what it attacks unsupported, which is the same move applied to a residual rather than to a doubt.
attrs.review_focus: Nineteen arguments is the measurement that made this its own round. Is there a cheaper first cut — typed residuals required only where the conclusion is PROVED and the argument is the SOLE leg?
attrs.statement: `remaining_trust` is non-authoritative commentary. If a residual can change whether an argument establishes its conclusion, it must be promoted into a typed object — an assumption, a defeater, a coverage obligation or an external premise — and referenced structurally; a settled argument may not rest on free text as an unstated premise.
